correctness.rationale: Using diag(1,-1,-1,-1), beta is effective (2E2+2E3+2D4+D2+D6), its six pairings are (2,1,1,2,1,1), and its anticanonical degree and one-point virtual dimension are both 8. The toric I-term with z prefactor is Q^beta z^(-7)/4 times [1-z^(-1) sum_i H_{D_i.beta} D_i+O(z^(-2))]. The divisor sum is (7/2)H-(1/2)E1-(3/2)E2-(3/2)E3. There is no positive-degree z^0 correction: for anticanonical degree 1 a nonnegative pairing vector would have to be a coordinate unit vector, but each unit vector violates at least one of k1+k2=k4+k5 and k2+k3=k5+k6, the two displayed divisor relations. A negative pairing gives a numerator factor D_i at m=0 and lowers the leading z-degree by at least one; degree at least 2 cannot contribute to z^0 either. Fano excludes nonzero effective classes of anticanonical degree 0. Thus after the standard classical divisor factor the small J coefficient of z^(-8), paired with H in the one-point insertion convention, is -7/8. H is self-dual, and 1/(z-psi) gives psi^7 at z^(-8). The result was checked by this derivation, not by trusting historical audit assertions; both named arithmetic scripts are present under source artifacts in this frozen package, even though the result's historical path note says they were absent from an earlier tree.
